2c0d1a694c08267b10bd793aba0279b9c7446483.message: Good, 10 percent fits the plan. Last question. Is there a date column that shows when each customer was observed, so we can test on recent customers only? I do not see an obvious one in the data. If there is none, we will treat the data as a single snapshot. Also, if you know roughly what a missed leaver costs you and what a wasted call costs, share it and I will add it.
2c0d1a694c08267b10bd793aba0279b9c7446483.user_text: We can call about 10 percent of customers each month.

c1a0a84a695c895f9f7245e490afcce40f7b698d.message: Thanks. I have added 3,000 customers a month, 60 dollars for a missed leaver and 3 dollars for a wasted call. There is no date column, so we will treat the data as a single snapshot and test on a random split. That is everything I need. Before we go on, please check one thing with your data team: if Complains or Status is filled in after a customer cancels, we should drop it, since it would make the results look better than they will be in real use.
c1a0a84a695c895f9f7245e490afcce40f7b698d.user_text: A lost customer is worth about 60 dollars a month, a wasted call costs 3 dollars. We have 3000 customers.

d5dd8ccd093db602e80c97e5a8667b3a204fb652.message: Churn is already set as the outcome, with 1 meaning the customer left. I suggest we aim to find the riskiest group of customers each month and call them first. The default is the top 10% of customers by risk. Is that a workable number of calls for your team, or should it be higher or lower? One thing to watch: Complains may be recorded close to the time a customer leaves, so it could be a possible leak. Status could be the same, if it changes when a customer cancels.
d5dd8ccd093db602e80c97e5a8667b3a204fb652.user_text: We want to know which customers are about to leave so we can call them first.
